raw_prompt: Make me a planter I can put on my wall.

ground_truth.prompt: Design a 3D-printable wall-mounted planter with the following specifications. The body is a hollow cylinder, 80 mm outer diameter, 90 mm tall, with a uniform 3 mm wall thickness, open at the top and closed at the bottom. The bottom of the cylinder contains four 3 mm diameter drainage holes arranged in a square pattern, each centered 15 mm from the cylinder's central axis. The back is a flat rectangular panel, 100 mm tall x 90 mm wide x 4 mm thick, tangent to the outside of the cylinder along a vertical line, and extending 5 mm above the cylinder's top edge and 5 mm below its bottom edge. The back panel contains one keyhole-shaped mounting slot centered horizontally. All external edges except the open top rim have a 1 mm fillet. The model is a single watertight solid suitable for FDM 3D printing without supports when oriented with the back panel flat on the print bed.
process_notes: Source: this is the exact, audited wall_planter prompt ladder from cadybara-kitchen/projects/wall-planter-cad-study/ (level 10, 'Fully Specified'), the only family in this project with a preserved, human-authored ground truth ladder.

Mounting slot is a keyhole cut into the back panel's face — not a clean through-hole for genus purposes on a normal print orientation reading, kept 'blind' in kind naming to avoid an unreliable through-hole count claim; recorded for prompt fidelity.
Drainage holes ARE clean through-holes (bottom face to cylinder interior) and are checked via the genus-based through-hole estimator.
